title: An over-long line is shortened from the end in the report and keeps the title
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Tech Story is off (Settings, then the Work Orders tab).
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with one labor line, line 1, titled "Replace tie rod" whose description is 0123456789 written 500 times in a row (5,000 characters; paste it in).
  • Have line 1 completed with no tech story, and work order 1 completed and invoiced today as invoice A.
  • Use Google Sheets (File, then Import, then Upload) to open downloaded files, so accented letters and character counts read correctly.
  • Start on Reports, then Export Reports in the Reports left menu, with the Export Report dialog open.
custom_steps:
1. Pick Customer Invoice in the Report Name list.
  2. Set the date range to today.
  3. Click Download.
  4. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets.
  5. In an empty cell, enter =LEN() with line 1's ItemDescription cell inside the brackets.
  6. In another empty cell, enter =RIGHT() with line 1's ItemDescription cell and 10 inside the brackets.
  7. In a third empty cell, enter =LEFT() with line 1's ItemDescription cell and 28 inside the brackets.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer Invoice is picked in Report Name.

Step 2:

  • The date range shows today's date.

Step 3:

  • A Customer Invoice file downloads.

Step 4:

  • Line 1's row (work order 1's invoice A) is there, and its ItemDescription cell is shorter than the full line of 5,018 characters (15 + 3 + 5,000).

Step 5:

  • The cell shows 4000: 15 characters of title + 3 for " - " + the first 3,982 characters of the description = 4,000. A digit or a plain letter takes one unit of the 4,000 limit, so 4,000 characters is exactly the limit.

Step 6:

  • The second cell shows "2345678901": the description was cut at its end (398 whole runs of 0123456789, then "01"), and no hyphen or space trails after it.

Step 7:

  • The third cell shows "Replace tie rod - 0123456789": the title survives whole, and the cut fell in the description.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 16 (27 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R8: “The values themselves are unchanged. Nothing is trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped that is not trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped today, other than the shortening described in S3-R7 and the removal of spaces and line breaks at the very end of the whole line (S3-R3), and the apostrophe in S3-R8a.”
  • S3-R4: “The same text is used by the live QuickBooks sync and by the downloadable Customer Invoice report. Built at the same moment, the two never show different text for the same line, apart from the leading apostrophe the report adds in S3-R8a. An invoice already in QuickBooks keeps its old text there (S3-N1, S3-E4).”
  • Key Decisions: “One builder serves both routes, and it stays that way. The live sync and the downloadable report read the same built line text. Fixing one place fixes both, and it is why the two routes cannot disagree about what a line says. Rejected: changing the report only, which was the original scope and would have left every live-integration shop, the population who actually complained, unfixed.”
  • Assumptions: “Intuit documents 4,095 for a QuickBooks Online line description without saying whether that counts characters or storage. The product carries its own limit of 4,000, which is under 4,095 on either reading, so the rule in S3-R7 is safe whichever it turns out to be. Establishing which unit Intuit means is worth one test against the sandbox someday, so the limit is chosen on evidence rather than on caution. It does not block this change.”
  • Assumptions: “A work order line's description can be far longer than that limit: ShopView allows 65,535 characters, against a 255-character line name. In practice descriptions are short phrases, so the cut is an edge case rather than a routine one.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.

The design's own words:

  • “The title leads the joined string, so whatever survives always begins with it. A shop that writes essays loses the tail of the essay, never the name of the job.”
